title: Paraphrase Recall Gap (PRG) v1 — pre-registration
hypothesis: KAOS memory search (SQLite FTS5 + porter stemming, no embeddings) misses a large fraction of paraphrased queries whose stored lesson exists. PRG measures that miss rate honestly and pins a control showing the instrument itself works. It is a measurement instrument, not a mechanism: its falsification is the control, and its purpose is to be the acceptance gate for any future paraphrase fix (issue #42).
setup: Fresh in-memory Kaos database per run. One agent is spawned; every stored_phrase is written with MemoryStore.write(type='insight', key='prg-<id>'). All 50 phrases are present simultaneously, so each acts as a distractor for the others.

query_modes.and: tokens joined by whitespace = FTS5 implicit AND. This is what `kaos memory search "<words>"` does today; it is the CLI-default condition and the headline.
query_modes.or: tokens joined by ' OR ' = lenient condition, reported alongside to show the ceiling of term-overlap retrieval.

hit_definition: A query is a hit when any of the top-5 MemoryEntry results has key == 'prg-<id>' of its own pair. Otherwise it is a miss.

metrics.headline: paraphrase/and/bm25 miss_rate
metrics.control: verbatim/and/bm25 miss_rate (the stored phrase itself, sanitized, as the query)
also_reported: p95 query latency ms per condition

gates.VOID: n_pairs < 50, OR control miss_rate > 0.10 (the instrument cannot even find verbatim text — broken bench, no claim may be made)
gates.ACCEPT: not VOID. The measurement stands and is published whatever the paraphrase miss rate is.
gates.REJECT: not applicable — PRG measures, it does not propose a mechanism. Any mechanism that claims to close the gap must pre-register its own gate against PRG (e.g. paraphrase/and/bm25 miss_rate <= 0.20 with control unchanged).

notes: Expected paraphrase/and miss rate before any fix: 80-90%. That expectation is recorded here so it cannot be retro-fitted.
